name: TUST micro magnetically guided helical r
full_name: TUST micro magnetically guided helical robot for guidewires (MMGHR): magnet in a helical casing with a soft structure ahead of a Nitinol guidewire, driven by a rotating field in a 3D Helmholtz coil
group: Tianjin Key Lab of Integrated Design and On-line Monitoring for Light Industry and Food Machinery and Equipment, College of Mechanical Engineering, Tianjin University of Science and Technology (P. Li, Z. Wang, C. Ye, D. Fang, J. Zhang); C. Liang, Dept. of Electronic Engineering, CUHK, and School of Mechanical Engineering, Tianjin University (li2024_helical p. 1)
group_short: Tianjin Key Lab of Integrated Design and
target_anatomy: 'vascular interventional surgery': guidewire navigation of curved blood vessel bifurcations (Abstract); stent and drug delivery named as potential uses (Sec. 6); tested in glycerin-filled Y-, Omega- and U-shaped tubes (6 mm inner diameter, 50 mm models) standing for the iliac artery, aortic arch and distal coronary arteries (Sec. 4.3, Fig. 15)
devices_driven: own guidewire head: radially magnetised cylindrical NdFeB magnet (2 mm diameter) in a titanium helical casing (pitch 1 mm, helix angle 20 deg), a silicone soft structure joining it to a Nitinol guidewire (about 100 mm long in the tests); the selected Robot-6 has d1 = 2 mm, d2 = 2 mm, d3 = 0.1 mm (Sec. 2.2.3, 4.1.1, Table 2, Fig. 10)
n_dof_detail: steering by the direction of the rotating field; helical propulsion by field rotation; no external feeding or twisting (Sec. 2.2, 5); DOF count N.R.
translation_detail: magnetic (helical propulsion: the casing turns with the external rotating field and advances the guidewire head, Sec. 2.2.3); no external feeding mechanism, 'relying exclusively on the propulsive force generated by the robot at the distal end' (Sec. 5)
rotation_detail: magnetic torque of the rotating field on the radially magnetised magnet turns the helical casing (Sec. 2.2.2, 2.2.3)
device_range: head 2 to 3 mm diameter, guidewire d3 0.1 or 0.2 mm, guidewire length 100 mm in vessel models; real guidewires are up to 1000 mm and out of scope (Table 2, Sec. 4.3, 5)
footprint_mm: 3D Helmholtz coil, coil radii 90 / 145 / 200 mm (x / y / z), turns 50 / 80 / 111 (Table 1); uniform working space 60 mm cube at 6 A (Sec. 2.1)
haptics_leader: none: field magnitude, direction and rotation frequency set in real time by the operator through LabVIEW with camera feedback (Sec. 3.1)
imaging_compat: optical: HIKVISION MV-CA016-10UM industrial camera above the coils (Sec. 3.1); fluoroscopy N.R.
sterility: N.R.; the discussion advises a thin biocompatible silicone coat over the magnet, silicone and titanium tip (Sec. 5)
validation_detail: bench: platform check with a T-shaped permanent magnet, max error < 3 deg (Sec. 3.2, Fig. 9); eight robot configurations in 6 mm tubes at 0 to 15 deg, liquid-free and glycerol-filled (Sec. 4.1.1, Figs. 10-12); steering at guidewire insertion lengths of 1, 2 and 3 cm with and without the soft structure (Sec. 4.2, Figs. 13-14); in vitro phantom: Y-, U- and Omega-shaped glycerin-filled tubes, selective, continuous and large-angle steering (Sec. 4.3, Figs. 15-19); repeat counts N.R.
key_numbers: soft structure raises the guidewire steering angle by 22 / 16 / 32 deg at 1 / 2 / 3 cm insertion, Robot-6 reaches 90 deg against 58 deg for Robot-5 (Sec. 4.2, Abstract); Robot-6 top speed 4.24 mm/s liquid-free and 2.9 mm/s in glycerol (Sec. 4.1.1); step-out frequency 10 Hz (2 mm heads) and 9 Hz (3 mm heads) in glycerol; 3 mT uniform field at 6 A (Sec. 2.1)
sim_model: none found for the robot; magnetic field of the coil system by Biot-Savart and COMSOL (li2024_helical Sec. 2.1, Figs. 2-3) and a torque relation T = m x B (Eq. 4)

sources.title: Development and verification of a micro magnetically guided helical robot with active locomotion and steering capabilities for guidewires

notes: REV4 2026-11-23: included after the full assessment of the 19 candidates (REV4_19_candidates.md §7). The robot is the guidewire's head: the paper does not feed the wire from outside and says so as the main limitation (Sec. 5). The field of 3 mT is much lower than the 15-20 mT of the other magnetic rows (coils built for a 60 mm workspace).
